_doc: The device layer's numbers, defined ONCE. Read by runtime/device.tsx, runtime/screen.tsx and runtime/gesture.tsx, and by scripts/device_script.py, scripts/device_geometry.py and scripts/screen_media.py. Values come from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-device-layer-design.md and the rulings in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-26-device-layer.md; the durations and caps are design choices to tune on real films, not measurements.

models._doc: REAL DEVICES, keyed to the screenshot they show. Every number under `published` was read on the page in `source` on the date in `retrieved` — never filled from memory. `screenMm` is not stored: both runtime/device.tsx and scripts/device_geometry.py derive it as px / ppi x 25.4, the size of the pixels themselves. Corner radii, the Dynamic Island, the notch, buttons and band are NOT published; each sits under `design` (a craft choice, drawn to read as the object) or `derived` (with how) — honest provenance, never a number dressed as a measurement. `px` is portrait (w, h) for watch/phone/tablet and landscape for a laptop. A screenshot is matched to a model by its exact pixel size (or that size divided by the model's point scale), see scripts/device_models.py.

derived.bezel: (caseMm - px/ppi*25.4)/2 per axis: 3.79 mm across, 3.68 mm down
derived.displayRadiusMm: 6.08 mm: the transparent corner mask of a 416x496 watchOS capture is a circle of 78 px (measured row by row: 39 px in at row 10, 16 at row 30, 5 at row 50, as a 78 px circle gives), 78/326 in

design.case: outer corner = display corner + bezel (concentric), a continuous-curvature outline; crown at 30% of the case height, side button at 63%; sport band 60% of the case width, tapering 10%

derived.bezel: (caseMm - px/ppi*25.4)/2 per axis: 3.93 mm across, 3.63 mm down
derived.displayRadiusMm: 6.08 mm x 374/416 = 5.47 mm: the 46 mm display's measured corner, scaled to this display's width

design.displayRadiusMm: corner not published: 14% of the display width, drawn to read as the product
design.island: Dynamic Island named on the spec page, size not published: 31% x 9.2% of the display width, 2.8% from its top
design.buttons: action + volume left, side + Camera Control right

design.displayRadiusMm: 14% of the display width, as the 6.3-inch

design.note: same pixels as the 18 Pro, so a 1206x2622 capture infers the Pro (listed first); name `model: "iphone-17"` to draw this one

design.camera: a dot centred on the long edge's bezel
design.buttons: not drawn: the iPad's top and volume buttons stand under half a millimetre proud of a 179.5 mm case — invisible at any size a film draws it

design.displayRadiusMm: not published: 5.2 mm, measured on the display corner of Apple's own iPad Pro App Store screenshots (a 33 px radius on a 1258 px-wide screen, scaled to 2064 px at 264 ppi) — the 11.5 mm generic estimate cut the status bar off those screens
design.camera: a dot centred on the long edge's bezel (the landscape top)
design.buttons: not drawn: under half a millimetre proud of a 215.5 mm case

macbook-air-13.name: MacBook Air 13-inch (M5)
macbook-air-13.notchSource: https://support.apple.com/en-us/102125 (MacBook Air with Liquid Retina display: camera housing built into the screen bezel)

derived.bezel: (304.1 - px/ppi*25.4)/2 = 6.9 mm at the sides; the lid's height is taken as the published depth (215 mm), so top + chin = 26.3 mm

design.topBezel: the top bezel equals the side bezel; the rest of the lid's height is the chin
design.displayRadiusMm: rounded corners at the top only (published), radius not published: 2.5 mm
design.notch: not sized on the page: 7% of the display width, as tall as the menu bar (3.5% of the display height)

_provenance.design: NOT measured on an Air: the 14-inch Pro's measured deck layout (keyboard well, trackpad, scoop, hinge) scaled to the Air's published width and depth; no speaker grilles are drawn beside the keyboard rather than inventing the Air's; lid thickness 3.6 mm of the published 11.3 is not published

macbook-pro-14.name: MacBook Pro 14-inch
macbook-pro-14.notchSource: https://support.apple.com/en-us/102125 (MacBook Pro with Liquid Retina XDR display)

derived.bezel: (312.6 - px/ppi*25.4)/2 = 5.1 mm at the sides; the lid's height is taken as the published depth (221.2 mm), so top + chin = 24.8 mm

design.displayRadiusMm: rounded at the top only (published): 2.5 mm

_provenance.published: case 312.6 x 221.2 x 15.5 mm (caseMm), 78/79 keys incl. 12 full-height function keys, Force Touch trackpad — https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/, read 2026-10-30
_provenance.derived: measured on https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_2021_14-inch_Silver_MacBook_Pro.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, Oops4321): the deck's four corners fitted to the published 312.6 x 221.2 mm and every other point mapped through that homography (±3 mm). keyboard well 14.6 mm in from each side, 17.7..130.1 mm from the back edge; trackpad 130.5 mm wide, 135.5..215.9 mm; thumb scoop 53.7 mm wide; speaker grilles 1.6..12.9 mm in from each side along the well; the deck's plan corner ~6 mm; the hinge slot ~37 mm in from each side. Cross-check: the screen's width on the same photo measures 302.0 mm against the published 3024 px / 254 ppi = 302.4 mm.
_provenance.design: the lid's thickness (4.9 mm of the published 15.5) is not published; the aluminium rim round the lid's black glass (0.8 mm) is drawn to read as the photo; the key layout is the ANSI MacBook Pro row pattern (14.5 units a row, full-height function row, inverted-T arrows) — legends as drawn on the photo
_provenance.notch: its height is the menu bar's: 3.5% of the display height (parts.notch.h) — a developer measured safeAreaInsets.top = 34 pt on a 14-inch M2 Pro (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/779268); Apple publishes no notch width, and the product draws a 200 pt stand-in when it cannot read the hardware's (src/crates/host/README.md), so the width stays design (parts.notch.w)

kinds._doc: The generic kinds: a screenshot no model matches is drawn on its KIND — the screen proportion in screenRatio, every bezel, radius and part in proportion to the `like` model (design: the kind's picture is that model's, stretched to the generic screen). A generic laptop draws no notch: it would cover the top of a screenshot from a machine that has none.

parts._doc: design — proportions of the parts no spec page publishes, in units of the SCREEN's width (watch band: of the case's width and height). Tuned by looking at 100% crops of real-material renders.

laptop3d._doc: design — the laptop's ONE camera (runtime/laptop3d.tsx). At rest it looks down restPitchDeg onto a lid opened to 90 + restPitchDeg, so the lid faces it square and the screen is exactly deviceGeometry's rect; cameraOfWidth is the camera's distance in case widths (a long lens: the deck's front edge draws ~11% wider than its back). The hinge offsets (the lid's chin drops 8 mm behind the base at the hinge: the photo shows ~10 mm of chin above the deck), key gap, lid's bottom corner and the light are drawn to read as the Wikimedia photo of a 14-inch MacBook Pro (refs in models.macbook-pro-14.body3d), not measured. maxYaw/maxPitch: the drawing orders the deck before the lid, which holds only while the camera is in front of the machine.
